schemeScope: Combined Paper 1 and Paper 2 scheme. PDF 16 reading marking instructions; 17–19 Léamhthuiscint A; 20–23 Léamhthuiscint B; 24 the literature Gaeilge note, 2A (question and the choose-two rule, no supporting notes) and 2B’s question; 25 2B’s choose-two rule; 26–27 poetry 3A and 3B; 28 Ceist 4 questions reprinted; 29 the Treoracha for 4A–4E (no text of their own) and 4F; 30 the general grading table for every total; 31 modified marking (SMM). PDF 1–15 belong to Paper 1; 32 empty.
reviewMethod: Every paper page (1 cover, 2 a pointer to the instructions, 3 instructions, 11 the 4F poem, 12 blank) and every applicable scheme page read in the text layer and checked against the printed page; the scheme’s symbol and Calibri glyphs read span by span against the rendered pages; each prompt and scheme slice is asserted against the PDFs by the builder.

nonPoolDecisions: Reading (2014: Léamhthuiscint A and B both compulsory): all twelve questions of both passages are carded as whole questions; each printed part is also a practice card at its published tariff. No part is priced “1 mharc + 1 mharc”, so there are no one-mark slots. A 1(a) (“3 mharc: 2 mharc + 1 mharc”), A 4(a), B 1(a), 2(a), 3(a) and 5(a) (“{2 mharc + 1 mharc}”) and both 6(a) stay whole as 0/2/3; A 2(a), 3(a), 5(a) and B 4(a) are single “{3 mharc}” answers with the partials the scheme prints.

A 6(b) prices two independent six-mark traits (“Tréith N ( 2 mharc) + Sampla N ( 4 mharc) ► 6 mharc”); B 6(b) two independent six-mark worries (“Ábhar imní N ( 2 mharc) + Cúis N ( 4 mharc) ► 6 mharc”); each half is also a practice slot. Both must be in the candidate’s own words.
Single-answer parts allow only the mark values the scheme prints for them (0, the printed partials, including deductions printed as “2-1” or “3-1”, and the full tariff).

Prose: 2A (Dís) and 2B (an optional short story) each ask for two of three printed headings; the scheme marks the better answer out of 13 and the other out of 12. Each is one card carrying all three headings, with the two Eolas marks and the shared Gaeilge 5 as criteria; no per-heading card, because a heading alone has no printed price. Poetry 3A and 3B and the six Q4 options are one card each; the optional text itself is open content chosen inside one route. 2014 prints no optional film or play.
sourceFindings: Paper 2 = 200: Ceist 1 Léamhthuiscint A 50 + B 50 (Q1–5 at 7 = (a) 3 + (b)(i) 2 + (b)(ii) 2; Q6 at 15 = (a) 3 + (b) 12); Ceist 2 Prós 30 (25 Eolas + 5 Gaeilge); Ceist 3 Filíocht 30 (25 + 5); Ceist 4 Litríocht Bhreise 40 (35 + 5).

Literature: the scheme prints no supporting notes for 2A or 2B (only the choose-two rule), no text of its own for 4A–4E (only the Ceist 4 Treoracha, “an t-eolas a mharcáil as 35 marc agus an Ghaeilge san iarracht a mheas as 5 mharc”), and no Gaeilge band table; PDF 30 “Grádú Marcála sna Ceisteanna” prints the grade-to-mark table for every total, lifted onto each literature card.

Grade-to-mark table: PDF 30 (printed page 28), on its own page after Ceist 4 and before the SMM page, headed “Grádú Marcála sna Ceisteanna”. Its N.B. tells the examiner to think in grades and percentages, to grade the answer first and then decide the mark, and points to the composition grading scheme “ar lch. eile”. It names no question: its columns are totals (200 … 5) with grade rows A–D. What ties it to Ceisteanna 2–4 is only its heading and its place in the Paper 2 section; the 25/13/12/35/5 columns are the literature tariffs.

Paper vs scheme: 3A prints (i) 15, (ii) 6, (iii) 9 and the scheme assesses Eolas 13 (“( Eolas = 13 mharc)”, no split), 5 (1 + 4), 7 (2 + 3 + 2); 3B (i) 13 (2 + 11), (ii) 5 (1 + 4), (iii) 7 (2 + 3 + 2); 4F prints (i) 20, (ii) 10, (iii) 10 and the scheme assesses Eolas 19 (2 + 17), 8, 8 (4 + 4); the remaining 5 is the shared Gaeilge award.

Scheme misprints and reprint differences kept as printed in the guidance (the card questions are the paper’s): B 1(b)(ii) is reprinted “(Alt 2)” (the paper: “(Alt 1)”); A 5(a) “ar an 27 Aibreán 1994?” (the paper: “ar 27 Aibreán 1994?”); B 1(a) “{2 mharc + 1mharc}”; 3A(i) drops “(thíos)”; 4F(i) drops “(thall)” and 4F(ii) reads “leis na línte ón dán” (the paper: “leis na línte seo”); the Ceist 4A–4E Treoracha print “usáid”.

Glyphs read from the font of every span and the rendered page: the reading answers’ list marks (Calibri-Bold, returned as U+0372, PDF 17–22) are read as “•”; the 6(b) panels’ arrows (TimesNewRomanPSMT, returned as “Ź”, PDF 19 and 23) as “►”; the SMM bullets (SymbolMT “x”, PDF 31) as “•”. The examiner’s score boxes inside the 6(b) panels (“T (1) + S (1) =”, “Á (2) + C (2) =” and the like) are removed by exact match.
